cefrAlignment: Suits B1: sentences of 3–18 words in predictable campus or service settings, and the teaching covers chunking, weak forms and basic intonation, which matches B1 phonological control and sustained repetition.
examFidelity: TOEFL Listen and Repeat is now described from exams.ts and the ETS practice test (a campus or academic situation, 7 sentences heard once, no prep, about 8–12 s to respond, getting longer). TOEIC Read a text aloud uses 45 s prep and 45 s reading, as in exams.ts.
fixes: Removed the unverified claim that TOEFL shows 'a picture of a place, such as a library or a museum'. The task description now follows ETS: a short scenario description, campus or academic settings, 7 sentences, no prep, about 8–12 s, sentences getting longer and more complex.
The TOEFL tip now says to read the scenario description, not 'look at the picture'.
Moved the ex2 museum tour into a university science museum, because ETS says the scenarios are academic or campus-related.
The ex4 shadowing line about the rooftop café now matches the ex5 read-aloud text (it was missing the opening hours). Renamed ex4 from 'chunks' to 'sentences' to say what it actually contains.
Softened the ex1 Q5 explanation ('You get credit for what you say accurately'): scoring details are not confirmed; it now says a mostly accurate repetition is better than silence.
The walkthrough now marks 'NOT CASH', matching the table's rule that negatives are strong, and says 'mental picture' so it is not confused with an on-screen picture.
openConcerns: The real TOEFL response window per sentence comes only from exams.ts ('about 8–12 seconds'). The shadow exercise does not time responses, so learners do not practise under that limit.
Intonation practice (lists rising and falling) depends on how browser TTS reads the lists. Someone should check them with common voices.
learnerOutcome: A learner can repeat campus-style sentences of up to about 18 words by remembering chunks and rhythm, and can read a short announcement aloud with sensible pauses, weak forms and list intonation.
